requirements.claim: Hey! Remember Hook? (110902) is Hook's damaging Skill action.
The un-enhanced Skill hits the designated enemy once per cast (3 casts in the fixture; the 4th Skill cast is enhanced by the Ultimate).
After the Ultimate, Hook's next Skill becomes the Enhanced Skill (110903/110909).
The Enhanced Skill is a Blast attack: it hits both adjacent enemies (2 adjacent hits from the fixture's single enhanced cast).
Boom! Here Comes the Fire! (110905) is delivered as a 30/70 two-hit split per Ultimate (2 Ultimates × 2 hits).
Hook's kit exposes Basic ATK, Skill (base and enhanced) and Ultimate as its action set; it never falls back to a generic attack action.
Hey! Remember Hook? L10 multiplier is 240% of ATK (110902 #1).
The Enhanced Skill primary hit L10 = 280% of ATK (110909 #1).
The Enhanced Skill adjacent hit L10 = 80% of ATK (110909 #5).
Boom! Here Comes the Fire! L10 total = 400% of ATK (110905 #1), first split part carries 30% → 1.2.
The Ultimate's second split part carries 70% of the 400% total → 2.8.
Oil to the Flames (110904) adds Fire DMG equal to the talent ladder value (L10 = 1.0×ATK) as an additional hit against Burned enemies.
Basic ATK (110901) runs the 50%→140% ladder (L10 = 140%); at the engine's default Basic Lv6 it totals 100% as a single hit.
Hook's Ultimate uses the 110-Energy ladder (sp_need 110); over this fixture her action set regenerates exactly 195 Energy (includes BA2's +5 Energy per Ultimate).
Every Skill cast applies the Burn debuff from 110902 #2 (4 Skill casts, 4 Burn applications).
Burn lasts #3 = 2 turns (110902).
Burn DMG = #4 = 65% of Hook's ATK at L10: baseDmg = 0.65 × 2560 effective ATK = 1664.
Burn ticks at the beginning of each enemy turn (110902: "at the start of each turn").
Bonus Ability Playing With Fire (BA2): after using the Ultimate, Hook's action is advanced by 20% (2 Ultimates → 2 advances).
Burn is applied during the Skill action and only ticks at the enemy's next turn start.
Hook's first Skill damage resolves before her first Ultimate damage in the fixture.
